title: 1996 AMC 8 Problem 8
statement: Points \(A\) and \(B\) are \(10\) units apart. Points \(B\) and \(C\) are \(4\) units apart. Points \(C\) and \(D\) are \(3\) units apart. If \(A\) and \(D\) are as close as possible, then the number of units between them is

solutions.text:
The distance is smallest when the points are collinear with \(C\) and \(D\) toward \(A:\) take \(A = 0,\) \(B = 10,\) \(C = 6,\) \(D = 3.\)

Then \(AD = 10 - 4 - 3 = 3.\)

Thus, the correct answer is B .
hints: Place all the points on one line so that \(C\) and \(D\) are pulled back toward \(A\)
With everything collinear, \(AD = AB - BC - CD\)
